A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ca2-VDM. All pages, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation-quality evaluations, ablations, timing measurements and computational-cost results in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds GPU-memory measurements, VBench scores and longer content-drift examples.

M1.justification: The causal temporal attention, prefix-enhanced spatial attention, shared caches, cache queue, Cyclic-TPEs and training objectives remain unchanged. The additional experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use InternVid, MSR-VTT, UCF101 and SkyTimelapse for the same generation and prediction tasks. V2 applies selected VBench metrics to the existing SkyTimelapse test set; it does not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Live2diff as an evaluated comparator in the new GPU-memory comparison, Table 6. Existing quality, timing and FLOPs comparators are retained; OS-Ext also participates in the added VBench comparison.

E3.justification: V2 substantially extends evaluation beyond the existing protocols: Table 6 measures cache and total memory with Live2diff at 4/50 denoising steps and Ca2-VDM at 50 steps, with and without prefix enhancement. Table 7 adds four VBench metrics at Pmax=25 and six autoregression steps. These are additional protocols; the original training, FVD and timing settings are retained.

E4.justification: The original condition-length and prefix-enhancement quality ablations remain. V2 adds memory comparisons across denoising-step counts and prefix-enhancement configurations, plus two SkyTimelapse content-drift cases displayed through frame 104 in Figure 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. The new memory statistics and VBench scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original FVD, timing and FLOPs results are retained. New Table 6 reports, for example, Ca2-VDM with prefix enhancement using 0.86 GB cache and 4.79 GB total memory. Table 7 adds four scores, all slightly below OS-Ext, including motion smoothness of 97.59 versus 98.93. Figure 12 adds content-drift findings. These substantially broaden reported evidence without establishing a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–8, including attention and training losses, are retained. V2 adds no theorem, proof or substantive derivation; its memory-scaling discussion explains the existing cache-sharing mechanism.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: causal generation removes redundant computation, cache sharing reduces storage, and generation quality remains competitive while inference becomes faster. The added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains Live2diff's timestep-dependent storage and explicitly qualifies the memory comparison as not strictly aligned because of architectural differences. Appendix E interprets the added cases as showing similar error accumulation to OS-Ext. The earlier substantive limitations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: Table 6 and its discussion add model-forward and cache tensor shapes, condition lengths, and Live2diff's batching relationship B=T. Existing training schedules, hyperparameters and code/evaluation-resource access information remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Live2diff and StreamDiffusion to contextualize the memory comparison, VBench for evaluation, and PTW watermarking in the impact statement. The main related-work discussion remains substantively unchanged; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence remain largely intact, with local wording and affiliation edits, author-date citations, and added acknowledgements and impact statement. Appendices are reorganized, including moving limitations from A to F. Appendix D.2 incorrectly retains the old Table 3/4 references after those tables exchange numbers.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICML formatting with different title, abstract, headers and table arrangements. V1 Figures 5 and 6 move to appendix Figures 9 and 10; new Tables 6–7 and Figure 12 are added, and Figure 11 expands an existing qualitative display. This is a substantial visual reorganization, although most original graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds direct evidence for the storage-efficiency claim and quantitative quality comparisons with OS-Ext, while showing longer-term degradation. These strengthen the paper, but the memory comparison uses differing architectures/settings and the additional quality evaluation remains confined to SkyTimelapse. Stale Table 3/4 references in Appendix D.2 introduce a small clarity regression. The net improvement is useful but limited.
